name: Left Ventricular Hypertrabeculation

criteria.description: Ratio of noncompacted to compacted myocardium > 2:1 at end-systole on echocardiography
Presence of prominent trabeculations and deep intertrabecular recesses communicating with the left ventricular cavity
No coexisting cardiac abnormalities that explain the hypertrabeculation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Both major criteria (trabeculation ratio > 2:1 and presence of prominent trabeculations with deep recesses) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI criteria may also be used as adjunctive diagnostic tools

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep intertrabecular recesses communicating with ventricular cavity

rare.notes: Due to thrombus formation in recesses

rare.symptomName: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing prominent trabeculations and deep recesses
Cardiac MRI confirming noncompacted to compacted myocardium ratio > 2.3
Left ventricular systolic dysfunction in advanced cases
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric and cytoskeletal genes (e.g., MYH7, ACTC1, TTN) in some familial cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including ventricular arrhythmias and conduction delays

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse ventricular dilation with reduced systolic function
Absence of prominent trabeculations and deep recesses
No deep intertrabecular recesses or excessive trabeculations

redFlags: Sudden onset of syncope or presyncope
Ventricular arrhythmias detected on ECG or Holter monitoring
references: Jenni R, Oechslin E, Schneider J, Attenhofer Jost C, Kaufmann PA. Echocardiographic and pathoanatomical characteristics of isolated left ventricular non-compaction: a step towards classification as a distinct cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2001;86(6):666-671.
Towbin JA, Lorts A, Jefferies JL. Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. Lancet. 2015;386(9995):813-825.

Kohli SK, Pantazis AA, Shah JS, et al. Diagnosis of left-ventricular non-compaction in patients with left-ventricular systolic dysfunction: time for a reappraisal of diagnostic criteria? Eur Heart J. 2008;29(1):89-95.
